feat(l10n): add Filipino (fil) localization (#4097)

* feat(l10n): add Filipino (fil) localization

Adds Filipino as a supported app locale to serve the Philippines (now
the 4th most popular country). All 1711 message keys outside the
known-untranslated debt set translated to natural Manila Filipino /
Taglish — informal pronouns (mo / ka / iyong), i- prefix verb pattern
for English-rooted actions, brand and tech terms (Divine, Nostr, NIP-05,
relay, video, feed, etc.) retained in English per modern Filipino mobile
app convention.

Translations were produced per-string by translators briefed on
brand-guidelines/TONE_OF_VOICE.md (Tone Dial — in-app UI: Rebel low,
Playful high) and verified against the existing 16-locale parity pass
(commit b5a666570). All ICU placeholders, plurals, and \\n newlines
preserved.

Locale registered in all four platform layers required by
test/l10n/platform_locale_declarations_test.dart:
- LocalePreferenceService.supportedLocales (Dart)
- android/app/src/main/res/xml/locales_config.xml
- ios/Runner/Info.plist (CFBundleLocalizations)
- ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj (knownRegions)

commit.message:
fix(security): iOS per-frame origin attestation for Nostr bridge (#3979)

* hardening(apps): iOS per-frame origin attestation for Nostr bridge (#3764)

The pigeon layer in webview_flutter_wkwebview 3.24.1 truncates
WKScriptMessage to name+body only; frameInfo is not plumbed to Dart.
This introduces a native Swift plugin that uses the package's public
external API (FWFWebViewFlutterWKWebViewExternalAPI) to look up the
WKWebView and replace the pigeon-managed WKScriptMessageHandler with a
FrameAttestingScriptMessageHandler that reads frameInfo.isMainFrame and
securityOrigin at the platform level.

The Dart sandbox screen activates attestation after addJavaScriptChannel
(which installs the JS alias window.divineSandboxBridge) and before the
first page load. On iOS, messages now arrive via EventChannel carrying
{message, isMainFrame, host, port, scheme}; _handleAttestedEvent rejects
any non-main-frame message with subframe_rejected before the nonce check
fires. Android is unchanged — nonce gate remains the effective defence
there; WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener is a follow-up.

Note: NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin.swift must be added to the Xcode
Runner target before building.

* chore(ios): add NostrBridgeAttestationPlugin.swift to Runner target

Adds the four required pbxproj entries (PBXBuildFile, PBXFileReference,
group child, Sources build phase) so the file compiles without a manual
Xcode step.

* fix(security): tighten iOS frame attestation per review feedback

- Single-instance enforcement: extract `NostrBridgeAttestationPolicy`
  state machine. Refuse a second `attach` with `ALREADY_ATTACHED`
  instead of silently overwriting the active eventSink — the previous
  shape was structurally broken under multiple sandbox WebViews.
- Observability: add `NSLog` on every native failure path
  (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `WEBVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `ALREADY_ATTACHED`) and a
  `Log.warning` on the Dart side when `PlatformException` trips the
  nonce-only fallback. The degraded posture is now visible in unified
  logs instead of silent.
- Drop `host` / `port` / `scheme` from the native event payload —
  Dart only consumes `message` + `isMainFrame`. Updated the Dart tests
  that simulated those keys to match the actual native contract.
- Move the document-start `WKUserScript` installation into the Swift
  plugin (new `bootstrapScript` arg on `attach`). Removes the
  `package:webview_flutter_wkwebview/src/common/web_kit.g.dart`
  private-path import, eliminating the Dart layer's only crossing of
  that boundary.
- Add native unit tests at `RunnerTests/RunnerTests.swift` covering
  the policy state machine (initial state, idempotent re-attach,
  cross-id refusal, detach semantics, re-attach after detach), the
  `eventPayload` dictionary shape (security-relevant key set, no
  origin-field leakage), and the `WKUserContentController` lifecycle
  the plugin depends on.

* fix(security): address review feedback on iOS frame attestation

- Switch the native-attestation fallback warning from LogCategory.auth to
  LogCategory.system: bridge-attestation availability is a platform/system
  channel concern, not an authentication flow.
- Move group-scoped mutable state (attestedEventHandler, capturedScripts)
  in the iOS frame attestation tests into an explicit setUp block, so each
  case starts from a known state without an implicit reset hidden inside
  pumpSandbox.

* fix(security): narrow subframe id-extraction catch to FormatException

The best-effort id-extraction block in `_handleAttestedEvent` previously
caught everything (`catch (_) {}`), which silently swallowed unrelated
invariant bugs (StateError, TypeError) on a security-relevant path.
Narrow the catch to `FormatException` (the only thing `jsonDecode`
throws here) and document the intent in the block body, matching the
existing `on FormatException` pattern used at five other jsonDecode
sites in `lib/`. No observable behaviour change; all 34 sandbox tests
pass unchanged. Addresses rabble's review nit.

* fix(security): log unexpected attestation event shape

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
feat(db): add outgoing_dms Drift table + DAO for durable DM queue (#3911)

* feat(db): add outgoing_dms Drift table + DAO for durable DM queue

Step 2 of the #3909 stack — adds the persistence layer for the durable
outgoing-DM queue. Pure data layer; no behavior change yet.

NIP-17 sends are two independent kind-1059 publishes (recipient gift
wrap + self-addressed gift wrap). The new `outgoing_dms` table tracks
each row with two independent status columns so a partial delivery
(recipient ✓, self ✗) can be retried on the missing wrap only — never
double-deliver to the recipient.

Schema highlights:
- `id` is the rumor event id (PRIMARY KEY) — stable across retries
  because `rumor_event_json` stores the serialized rumor and retries
  re-wrap the same one (rumor.id is a hash of its fields, so re-mint
  would break receiver-side dedup).
- `recipient_wrap_status` and `self_wrap_status` are independent
  string-encoded enums (`pending` | `sent` | `failed`). String form
  lets us add new states (e.g. `cancelled`) without a schema bump.
- `retry_count`, `last_error`, `last_attempt_at` mirror PendingActions
  for the retry service to drive backoff.
- `owner_pubkey` for multi-account isolation, mirroring
  `direct_messages.owner_pubkey`.
- Indexes for the access patterns the queue + retry service need:
  per-conversation watch, per-wrap-status retry sweeps, queued-at
  ordering.

Schema version stays at 1 — registered via the existing
`_createMissingTables` runtime CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS pattern from
`personal_reposts` and `nip05_verifications`. No formal Drift
migration to write; existing installs get the table on next launch.

DAO mirrors PendingActionsDao:
- `enqueue` (insertOnConflictUpdate so retry-enqueue is a no-op)
- `markRecipientWrapStatus` / `markSelfWrapStatus` (independent)
- `incrementRetry`, `deleteById`
- `getById`, `watchForConversation`, `watchAllForOwner`,
  `getRetryableForOwner` (filters by max-retry cap),
  `getStillPendingForOwner` (recovers from app-kill mid-publish)

Domain model `OutgoingDm` exposes `isFullyDelivered` (both wraps sent)
and `hasRetryableFailure` (either wrap failed) as derived getters so
callers don't reason about the two enums by hand.

Tests: 20 DAO tests covering CRUD, both wrap-status transitions
independently, retry-cap filtering, owner-pubkey isolation, partial
vs fully-delivered semantics, watch-stream emissions on insert /
update / delete.

Relates to #3909

* fix(db): tighten outgoing_dms DAO contract from review (#3911)

Addresses review #4216718908 on the outgoing_dms foundation:

- enqueue is now a true no-op on duplicate id via INSERT OR IGNORE.
  insertOnConflictUpdate would have overwritten in-flight delivery
  state (per-wrap status, retry_count, last_error, published wrap
  event ids) on a re-enqueue, defeating idempotency.
- _parseStatus throws UnknownOutgoingWrapStatusException on
  unrecognised persisted status strings instead of coercing them
  back to pending. Coercion would silently re-activate corrupt or
  future-schema rows in the retry sweep and risk double-delivery.
- Adds an upgrade-path test that drops outgoing_dms, reopens the
  database, and asserts the runtime CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS path
  recreates the table + indexes and the DAO works end-to-end —
  covers existing installs that bypass Drift's m.createAll().

* feat(db): add OutgoingDmsDao.clearAllForUser for signout isolation

Mirrors `DirectMessagesDao.clearAllForUser` so the signout / account-
switch path can drop a logged-out user's outgoing-DM queue rows in a
single statement. Without this, the durable retry service introduced
later in the #3909 stack would otherwise pick up the previous user's
in-flight rows after re-login under a different account and try to
publish them under the new signer.

Pure addition; no callers yet — the repository hooks into this in a
follow-up commit. Two tests cover the happy path (only matching owner
deleted) and the no-op return-zero case.

* fix(db): tighten outgoing_dms from second-round review (#3911)

Addresses three blockers from NotThatKindOfDrLiz's CHANGES_REQUESTED on
3b072e9 and the timestamp verify-or-fix from rabble.

B2 (per-wrap last_error) — split the shared `last_error` column into
`recipient_wrap_last_error` and `self_wrap_last_error`. The two wrap
state machines transition independently, so collapsing both error
channels into one column silently overwrote the earlier reason on the
second failure (recipient relay rejection then self-relay timeout left
only the latter visible). New test in `outgoing_dms_dao_test.dart`
proves a recipient failure followed by a self failure preserves both
error strings independently.

B4 (last_attempt_at codec mismatch) — `incrementRetry` was writing
`Variable<int>(DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch)` via raw SQL,
but Drift's int DateTime codec stores seconds-since-epoch
(`store_date_time_values_as_text: false` in `drift_schema_v1.json:7`),
so reads decoded the value ~1000x in the future (year ~57311). Replaced
with a typed `update().write()` inside a transaction so the codec is
the single writer — matches `markRecipientWrapStatus` /
`markSelfWrapStatus`. Existing test only asserted non-null; added
wall-clock window assertion (±2s) so a future regression to a raw-SQL
writer fails the test loudly instead of returning a year-57000 stamp.

B3 (FIFO ordering not pinned) — `getRetryableForOwner` and
`getStillPendingForOwner` order by `queuedAt`, but the tests used
`unorderedEquals` and identical `queuedAt` defaults. Inserted rows
with explicit, distinct `queuedAt` values (in reverse insertion order
so the assertion can't pass by accident) and replaced `unorderedEquals`
with ordered `equals` — locks FIFO before the retry service depends on
it.

B1 (schema parity) — added a `schema parity` test in
`app_database_test.dart` that captures `pragma table_info` and the
non-autoindex names from a Drift `m.createAll()` install vs a
drop+reopen runtime CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS install, asserting both paths
produce the same column tuples and the same index set. Caught a real
pre-existing bug along the way: the runtime CREATE INDEX statements
sat inside the "if table missing" block, so a Drift-created fresh
install had the table but none of its indexes (the
`List<Index> get indexes` getter on `OutgoingDms` is documentation —
the project doesn't wire it through `@DriftDatabase(indexes: ...)`).
Hoisted the four `outgoing_dms` index statements outside the
"if missing" block so the runtime path is the canonical creator on
both new and existing databases. Now both paths emit the same shape
and the parity test passes.

* refactor(dm): factor NIP17MessageService into buildRumor + sendRumor (#3911)

DmRepository.sendMessage needs to enqueue an outgoing_dms row with
the rumor's id as PK BEFORE publishing — otherwise a publish that
succeeds with the recipient relay but the app crashes before
sendPrivateMessage returns leaves no local trace of the in-flight
send, defeating the queue's whole crash-recovery contract.

The existing sendPrivateMessage built the rumor inline and only
exposed its id in the result, making this impossible. Carved the
construction out as a pure buildRumor() returning the unsigned Event,
and the publish-and-wrap step as sendRumor(rumorEvent, recipientPubkey)
taking a pre-built rumor. sendPrivateMessage stays as a convenience
wrapper that delegates to both, so existing callers (sendGroupMessage,
sendFileMessage, the NIP-04 fallback path) keep working unchanged.

Five new tests cover the split: buildRumor doesn't touch the relay,
the rumor id surfaced from buildRumor matches the one returned by
sendRumor (the queue PK depends on this), additional tags land after
the recipient p-tag, kind 15 file rumors are buildable, and the
sendPrivateMessage convenience smoke test still passes.

Per-wrap publish status (NIP17SendResult.selfWrapPublished from #3910)
is still tied to overall result.success in this refactor — when #3910
merges, the next commit on the queue wiring will switch the repo from
"mark both wraps from result.success" to per-wrap precision.

* feat(dm): rewire sendMessage through outgoing_dms queue (#3911)

Addresses the "no inert infrastructure" blocker from
NotThatKindOfDrLiz's CHANGES_REQUESTED — DmRepository.sendMessage
now uses the outgoing_dms queue end-to-end, exercising every DAO
contract pinned by the data layer:

  enqueue ──▶ buildRumor ──▶ sendRumor
                                 │
                  ┌──── success ──┴──── failure ────┐
                  ▼                                 ▼
       transaction(                          markRecipientWrapStatus(failed)
         insertMessage,                      markSelfWrapStatus(failed)
         upsertConversation,                 (row stays for retry service)
         deleteById                          (no direct_messages insert)
       )

Two-step build (buildRumor + sendRumor in commit 7b3527c7a)
makes pre-publish enqueue possible — the queue PK is the rumor
event id, which the receiver-side gift-wrap dedup keys on, so it
must be stable across the publish boundary. Building the rumor in
the repo and reusing it for the publish keeps that contract.

Per-wrap precision is still tied to overall result.success — pre
PR #3910's NIP17SendResult.selfWrapPublished. When #3910 lands,
the failure-path mark calls split: recipient gets result.success ?
sent : failed and self gets result.selfWrapPublished ? sent :
failed, surfacing the partial-delivery state the table was built
for.

OutgoingDmsDao is an optional named DmRepository parameter so the
9 pre-existing test fixtures keep passing without rewiring; the
production dmRepositoryProvider now passes db.outgoingDmsDao.
Three new tests cover the wiring:
  - enqueue + delete on success (queue PK stays consistent)
  - mark both wraps failed on publish failure (no DM inserted,
    no row deleted)
  - opt-in: no DAO injected ⇒ queue is never touched

Existing 126 dm_repository tests stay green via a setUp bridge
that forwards sendRumor stubs to sendPrivateMessage so the
existing verify(...sendPrivateMessage(...)) assertions still
match the rewired flow.

* feat(dm): clear outgoing_dms queue on destructive signout (#3911)

Hooks the OutgoingDmsDao.clearAllForUser method shipped in a3c854661
into UserDataCleanupService.onDatabaseCleanup, alongside the existing
pendingActionsDao.clearAll(userPubkey) call.

Without this, a destructive signout (account delete or identity
change) would leave the previous user's queued sends in the database;
when a different account later signs in and the retry service comes
online, it would try to re-publish those rows under the new signer.
The clear is gated on deleteUserData=true since the rows are already
owner-scoped by ownerPubkey, so an account switch (non-destructive
signout) doesn't need the wipe — the new user's queries naturally
filter the previous user's rows out.

Wraps the call in safeDelete so a transient DB error during cleanup
doesn't block the rest of the destructive-signout sequence, mirroring
the pattern used for drafts/clips/pendingUploads/personalReactions/
personalReposts/pendingActions immediately above it.

* fix(dm): preserve queued partial deliveries

merges, the next commit on the queue wiring will switch the repo from

now uses the outgoing_dms queue end-to-end, exercising every DAO

match the rewired flow.

into UserDataCleanupService.onDatabaseCleanup, alongside the existing

personalReposts/pendingActions immediately above it.

fix(dm): surface NIP-17 self-wrap publish failure via NIP17SendResult (#3910)

* fix(dm): surface NIP-17 self-wrap publish failure via NIP17SendResult

NIP-17 sends two independent gift wraps to relays: one to the recipient
and one to the sender's own pubkey. The self-addressed wrap is what
makes the sender's own messages recoverable on reinstall, second-device
login, or fresh account state — without it, the recipient sees the
message but the sender does not on any other device.

`NIP17MessageService.sendPrivateMessage` published the recipient wrap,
then attempted the self-wrap inside a swallow-all `try { … } catch (e)
{ Log.error('Self-wrap failed (non-fatal): $e'); }`. That branch had
three failure paths — `getGiftWrapEvent` returned null, `publishEvent`
returned null, or the call threw — and the result type carried no
signal that any of them happened. Both `success: true with self-wrap
landed` and `success: true with self-wrap dropped` returned the same
`NIP17SendResult.success(...)`.

This is the F3 of the #3902 investigation. Without it, the durable
outgoing-message queue (#3909) cannot tell "fully delivered" from
"delivered to recipient only" and would either re-publish to the
recipient (double-deliver) or drop the row (sender's own history
silently rots).

- `NIP17SendResult` gains a `selfWrapPublished` field, defaulting to
  `true` so existing callers that don't yet care about per-wrap status
  are unaffected. Documented as only meaningful when `success: true`.
- `NIP17MessageService.sendPrivateMessage` now tracks the self-wrap
  outcome across all three failure paths and propagates it in the
  result. The catch still swallows (recipient was delivered) but logs
  with category-appropriate severity.
- New test pins the partial-delivery path: recipient-success +
  self-wrap-throws now returns `selfWrapPublished: false` (was
  unobservable before this change). Adds the "publishEvent returns
  null without throwing" case which was previously indistinguishable
  from the success path. Updates the prior test that pinned the
  swallow-all behavior — that was pinning the bug.
- Adds `nip17_send_result_test.dart` covering the success-default,
  explicit-false, and failure-branch field behavior.

Relates to #3909

* test(dm): cover self-wrap publish branches with valid sender pubkey

The self-wrap publish lines added in this PR (the inner publishEvent
call and its returns-null branch) were unreachable from the existing
test setup because the synthetic _testPublicKey is not a valid
secp256k1 point — the self-wrap's NIP-44 ECDH throws before the
publish call is reached, so coverage on the package dropped to
92.78% (gate is 93%).

Add a nested group that pairs LocalNostrSigner(_testPrivateKey)
with a sender pubkey actually derived via getPublicKey(), so the
self-wrap path runs end-to-end and we can drive both the
both-publishes-succeed branch and the self-wrap-publish-returns-null
branch from the mock relay client. Brings package coverage back to
93.04%.

* refactor(models): make NIP17SendResult.selfWrapPublished nullable

Address PR #3910 review (thread r3178622358): on the failure branch,
`selfWrapPublished` previously defaulted to `true`, exposing a concrete
success-like value on a result where the self-wrap is by definition
not attempted. With no production consumers downstream yet, this is
the right window to tighten the type before more callers depend on it.

- Field type changes from `bool` to `bool?`. The const constructor's
  default flips from `true` to `null`, so a direct `const NIP17SendResult(
  success: false, error: ...)` now produces `selfWrapPublished: null`
  rather than a misleading `true`.
- The `success(...)` factory keeps its `bool selfWrapPublished = true`
  parameter for backward compatibility with existing call sites that
  do not pass per-wrap status.
- The `failure(...)` factory keeps its current shape and lets the
  null default flow through — type encodes "not applicable on this
  branch."
- Class-level dartdoc reworded to drop the "(the DM outgoing-message
  queue) act on `selfWrapPublished` separately" forward reference;
  the queue (#3909) is not on `main` yet. Field dartdoc reworded to
  describe the surfaced state and to flag #3909 as the future home
  of retry handling without promising it as current behavior.
- Failure-branch model test updated: now asserts `selfWrapPublished
  is null` instead of pinning the soon-to-be-old `true` default.

No production consumers read `selfWrapPublished` outside this PR, so
no call-site migration is needed. Verified via `flutter analyze
packages/models packages/dm_repository lib test integration_test` and
the full `dm_repository` + `models` test suites.

Relates to #3909

* fix(dm): clarify self-wrap log copy and inject GiftWrapBuilder for tests

Addresses PR #3910 review threads r3178622356 (log/doc wording) and
r3178622359 (untested defensive null-event branch).

Wording (r3178622356): the prior block comment and three log lines
forward-referenced an "outgoing queue" that "will retry" the missing
self-wrap publish. That queue is the next PR in the #3909 stack and
is not on `main` yet, so the wording over-promised behavior that does
not exist. Reworded to describe the surfaced state ("recipient was
delivered, but the sender will not see this message on other devices
or after a reinstall") instead of asserting a future remediation. The
block comment retains a single `(see #3909)` breadcrumb framed as
"future retry handling must target only the self-wrap" rather than as
a runtime promise.

Test seam (r3178622359): the `selfWrapEvent == null` branch in
`sendPrivateMessage` was previously unreachable from the test surface
because `GiftWrapUtil.getGiftWrapEvent` is a static call — synthetic
test keys force the call to throw inside NIP-44 ECDH (covering the
catch path) and real test keys return a non-null event (covering the
success path), but neither setup exercises the in-between case where
the SDK declines to produce an event without throwing.

- New `GiftWrapBuilder` typedef matching the static signature.
- Optional `@visibleForTesting` constructor parameter on
  `NIP17MessageService` defaulting to `GiftWrapUtil.getGiftWrapEvent`,
  threaded through to a private `_giftWrapBuilder` field. Production
  call sites for both the recipient wrap and the self-wrap call go
  through the field, keeping them symmetric — a future test that
  needs to mock the recipient wrap will not require another refactor.
- New test in the "with sender pubkey derived from signer key" group
  injects a builder that delegates to the real `GiftWrapUtil` for the
  first call (so the recipient wrap is a real kind-1059 event flowing
  into the publish path) and returns null on the second call,
  exercising the previously-untested branch and asserting
  `success: true, selfWrapPublished: false`.

Verified: `dart format`, `flutter analyze packages/models
packages/dm_repository lib test integration_test`, the full
`dm_repository` test suite (185 tests passing), and
`conversation_bloc_test.dart` (NIP17SendResult consumer) all clean.

Relates to #3909

* refactor(dm,models): drop "outgoing queue" forward-refs in tests; add direct builder-throws test

Self-review of #3910's prior commits caught two consistency gaps:

1. The "queue retries / outgoing queue can retry" wording NotThatKindOfDrLiz
   asked us to remove from production logs and dartdocs (r3178622356) was
   only cleaned up in `lib/`. Four lines in the test files still over-
   promised: a test description, an inline comment, an assertion `reason`
   in `nip17_message_service_test.dart`, and the ABOUTME header in
   `nip17_send_result_test.dart`. These bleed into CI test output and
   `grep` results, so they get the same treatment as the production
   code — describe the surfaced state, defer the queue to (#3909).

2. The existing `'self-wrap publish throws'` test (line 224) drives the
   throw via the synthetic `_testPublicKey`, which is not a valid
   secp256k1 point — the throw originates inside `GiftWrapUtil.getGift
   WrapEvent`'s NIP-44 ECDH, not the mocked `publishEvent`. A future
   SDK change could shift where the throw fires and silently break the
   test's intent without breaking its name.

   Add a sibling test in the `with sender pubkey derived from signer key`
   group that uses the `@visibleForTesting GiftWrapBuilder` injection
   seam to throw at a known point. The catch path is now verified
   independently of SDK internals; the synthetic-key test stays as a
   positive-control integration check.

Verified: `dart format` clean, `flutter analyze packages/models
packages/dm_repository` clean, full `nip17_message_service_test.dart`
suite (16 tests, +1 new) passing, `nip17_send_result_test.dart` (6 tests)
passing.

* refactor(dm,models): tighten package boundaries and pin success-only invariant

Three small follow-ups from self-review of #3910's prior commits:

- Swap `package:flutter/foundation.dart` for `package:meta/meta.dart`
  in `nip17_message_service.dart`. Per `architecture.md`, the
  repository layer "should not import any Flutter dependencies."
  `dm_repository.dart` still imports `flutter/foundation` for its own
  reasons (pre-existing), but the new `@visibleForTesting` annotation
  added in 686796de5 didn't need to drag Flutter into a fresh import.
  `nostr_client/relay_manager.dart` already follows this convention
  for the same `@visibleForTesting` pattern. Adds `meta: ^1.17.0` as
  a direct dependency in `dm_repository/pubspec.yaml` to avoid relying
  on transitive resolution.

- Annotate the `GiftWrapBuilder` typedef with `@internal`. The typedef
  is purely a test-seam concept — production code never references it
  by name. The `dm_repository.dart` barrel re-exports
  `nip17_message_service.dart`, so without `@internal` the typedef
  leaked into the package's public API; the analyzer caught this with
  `invalid_export_of_internal_element`. Resolved by adding `hide
  GiftWrapBuilder` to the barrel's export. Tests inside the package
  use inline closure syntax and don't reference the typedef by name,
  so they are unaffected.

- Add an invariant `assert` to `NIP17SendResult`'s const constructor
  so `const NIP17SendResult(success: true)` (without `selfWrapPublished`)
  fails at construction in checked mode. The dartdoc already says the
  field is "meaningful only when success is true," but the const
  constructor previously let a hand-built result silently violate
  that. The factories (`success(...)`, `failure(...)`) already produce
  conformant results; the only direct const usage in the codebase
  (`bug_report_worker_api_test.dart:147`) sets `success: false` and
  the assert allows that case (`!success` short-circuits). Production
  runtime is unaffected — `assert` runs only in checked mode.

Verified: `dart format` clean, `flutter analyze packages/models
packages/dm_repository lib test integration_test` clean, full
`packages/models` and `packages/dm_repository` test suites green
(186 + 6 tests), `conversation_bloc_test.dart` and
`bug_report_worker_api_test.dart` (NIP17SendResult consumers) green.

* test(dm): assert partial-delivery log line on self-wrap failure

Closes the gap from PR #3910's manual-verification checklist: the
reviewer asked for a real-device confirmation that
`Successfully published NIP-17 message (selfWrapPublished=false)`
fires on partial delivery (Keycast RPC slow -> self-wrap second
sign throws). Pinning the exact log copy via LogCaptureService gives
permanent CI coverage instead of relying on a Keycast-slow setup
per cycle. Adds a symmetric assertion on the =true branch.

* refactor(models): make NIP17SendResult invariant unrepresentable via sealed class

Reviewer flagged that the success-with-null-selfWrapPublished invariant
was enforced only by `assert` (debug-only) and that release builds
could still construct an invalid result. Convert NIP17SendResult to a
sealed class with NIP17SendSuccess (selfWrapPublished required,
non-null) and NIP17SendFailure (no selfWrapPublished field) subclasses.
Factories preserved on the base, so all 66 factory call sites and 53
field readers stay unchanged.

Reword two log-pinning test reasons in nip17_message_service_test.dart
to drop the "outgoing queue will key off this string" framing — the
queue keys off NIP17SendResult.selfWrapPublished. Logs stay diagnostic.

Migrate the one bare-constructor caller in bug_report_worker_api_test
to NIP17SendResult.failure(...). Apply prefer_const_constructors at
the call sites that became const-eligible once the failure factory
became const.

Addresses review 4244268462 on PR #3910.

* test(dm): fix publish-result stubs after rebase

* fix(dm): handle sealed self-wrap status in conversation bloc

* style(dm): format nip17 message service test

* fix(dm): const failure result in nip04 send path

fix(dm): clear optimistic on send failure, surface retry, key bloc on repo identity (#3908)

* fix(dm): clear optimistic on send failure, surface retry, key bloc on repo identity

When an outgoing DM fails (relay reject, slow Keycast RPC, signer error,
DB-persist throw), the ConversationBloc only flipped `sendStatus` to
`failed` and left the optimistic message in `state.messages`. The watch
stream was the sole mechanism that ever removed the optimistic — so on
failure it lingered until the bloc was disposed, then vanished on
re-entry. That reproduces the user's report exactly: "looks sent, then
disappeared when I came back."

Three coordinated changes:

- bloc: strip the optimistic for the failed `pendingId` and record a
  `FailedSend(content, recipientPubkeys)` in state. A new attempt
  clears `lastFailedSend` so the SnackBar can't refire from a stale
  failure.
- view: `BlocListener` on `sendStatus → failed` shows a localized
  SnackBar (`dmSendFailedMessage`) with a Retry action that
  redispatches `ConversationMessageSent` from `lastFailedSend` — UI
  doesn't hold non-UI state.
- page: `BlocProvider<ConversationBloc>` now carries
  `key: ValueKey((dmRepository, currentPubkey))`, mirroring the four
  canonical sites (`video_feed_page.dart`, `pooled_fullscreen_video_
  feed_screen.dart`). Without it, a `dmRepository` captured during a
  brief unauthenticated window scopes all reads/writes by an empty
  `_userPubkey` for the lifetime of the bloc, an independent path to
  the same disappearance symptom.

Tests:
- bloc: pinned `messages: isEmpty` and `lastFailedSend` invariants on
  every failure path; added retry round-trip + state lifecycle tests.
- view: 3 new SnackBar tests (shown on failure, not on success, retry
  redispatches with captured content + recipients).
- page: new `conversation_page_repo_swap_test.dart` mirroring
  `pooled_video_feed_item_repo_swap_test.dart` — recreate-on-flip,
  preserve-on-equal-identity, intentional-state-loss-on-flip.

Closes #3902

* test(l10n): record #3908 dm-send-failure keys in untranslated-debt list

`dmSendFailedMessage` and `dmSendFailedRetry` were added to `app_en.arb`
on this branch without translations. The ARB-consistency test correctly
treats that as drift and fails on the synthetic merge ref.

Adds the two keys to `_knownUntranslatedDebt` with a provenance comment,
matching the established pattern used for every other batch of deferred
translations in this set. Non-English locales fall back to English until
the next translation pass. No app code changes.

* fix(dm): make optimistic pendingId collision-safe (#3908 review)

The failure-cleanup path strips optimistic rows by `m.id != pendingId`,
so the strip's correctness depends on every optimistic row in
`state.messages` having a unique id. The original implementation derived
`pendingId` from a second-resolution timestamp, which collides on rapid
sends — two attempts within the same wall-clock second share an id, and
when the second one fails the cleanup removes both pending rows along
with its own.

Replace the timestamp with a UUID v4 (already in `pubspec.yaml`,
`uuid: ^4.5.1`, used by `BugReportService`). To keep the new contract
testable without depending on real wall-clock timing, expose a
`@visibleForTesting` `pendingIdFactory` constructor parameter that
defaults to a UUID-backed factory.

Adds a regression blocTest that drives two sends through `sequential()`
— the first succeeds (so its optimistic stays in `state.messages`
during the production window where `watchMessages` has not yet emitted
the persisted row), and the second fails. Pins:

  - the second's pending id differs from the first's,
  - the failure cleanup strips only the second's row,
  - the first's optimistic survives in `state.messages`,
  - `lastFailedSend` records only the failing attempt's content.

Under the old timestamp-based id this final state would be `messages:
isEmpty`. Under the new factory it is `messages: [pending-1]`.

define both keys.

on async visible state changes — including when a SnackBar appears.

than the written rule, so reviewer asked for an explicit announce.

mirroring the existing precedent in `feed_auto_advance_cubit.dart`)

deliver through) and pins:

    siblings.

Reviewer flagged that `DmRepository.sendMessage()` returned `success: true`
even when the recipient gift wrap landed but the sender's self-addressed
NIP-17 gift wrap silently failed to publish. `_onMessageSent()` only
checked `result.success`, so this branch never surfaced to the UI and
never became retryable — the sender's other devices would not see the
message on relay-only restore, but the conversation would happily flip
to `SendStatus.sent` and the user had no signal anything was wrong.

- `NIP17SendResult` gains `selfWrapPublished` (defaults to `true`, set
  explicitly by the success factory). `NIP17MessageService` now checks

  `false` whenever the inner `publishEvent` returned null or threw.

  emits `sentPartial` plus a `lastFailedSend` snapshot when any
  successful per-recipient send had its self-wrap fail (in 1:1 there is
  one; in groups, every-recipient must self-wrap to count as full
  success). The optimistic stays — the message *was* delivered and
  `DmRepository` already persisted it locally — so the UI does not
  flicker between visible and stripped while `watchMessages` catches up.

  `dmSendPartialMessage`. Retry reuses `dmSendFailedRetry`. Tapping
  Retry redispatches the full `ConversationMessageSent`, which double-
  delivers to the recipient on success — accepted tradeoff against
  silent loss of cross-device sync, and the principled fix (durable
  outgoing queue with self-wrap-only retry) is tracked in #3909.

- `NIP17MessageService`: tightened the existing throws test to also
  pin `selfWrapPublished == false`, and added a returns-null test that
  mirrors the silent-failure shape the reviewer called out.
- `ConversationBloc`: 1:1 partial-delivery test pins the optimistic-
  preserved + `sentPartial` + `lastFailedSend` contract; group test
  pins the every-self-wrap-must-succeed group rule.
- `ConversationView`: distinct partial SnackBar test pins the
  localized partial copy is rendered (not the failure copy) and Retry
  is offered.

translated in the follow-up i18n commit so the diff stays reviewable.

The sibling BlocProvider already keyed in this PR (#3908) covers

commit.message:
fix(clip-manager): treat post-deletion cleanup as best-effort (#4085)

The CI flake on PR #4078 (`fix/top-align-square-videos`, completely
unrelated to ClipManager) caught a latent fragility in
`removeClipById`: after the synchronous state mutation and
forced autosave, the method reads `databaseProvider` and runs
`FileCleanupService.deleteRecordingClipFiles`. Either step can throw
in a test environment that doesn't override `databaseProvider` or
in production if Drift / sqlite has a transient init hiccup, and the
throw rejected the whole future — turning a successful delete into
an apparent failure.

Wrap that tail in try/catch + Log.error so disk-side failures stay
out of the caller's contract. The clip is already gone from state
and the autosave above persists that; cleanup is best-effort.

Add a regression test that pins the contract: `removeClipById`
returns true and leaves state empty even when the test container
provides no database override.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

`flutter = "3.41.4-stable"`; mise's flutter plugin appends `-stable`
itself, producing the 404 archive name `flutter_macos_arm64_3.41.4-stable-stable.zip`.
Drop the suffix and bump to the latest stable in the 3.41 line.

Aligns three previously divergent pins on 3.41.9:
- mobile/mise.toml             (was 3.41.4-stable, broken URL)
- .github/workflows/*          (was 3.41.4)
- codemagic.yaml               (was 3.41.1)

Bumps Dart SDK 3.11.1 -> 3.11.5 (also patch-only). Pubspec caret
constraints (`^3.41.1`, `sdk: ^3.11.0`) are already satisfied, so no
package changes are required and `pubspec.lock` is unchanged.

Verified locally on 3.41.9: `mise install` succeeds, `flutter analyze
lib test integration_test` is clean, and the ClickableHashtagText test
suites pass.

commit.message:
l10n(category-gallery): translate sort labels and clear from debt (#4064)

The 5 categoryGallerySort* keys ("Category sort options", "Hot",
"New", "Classic", "For You") sat in `_knownUntranslatedDebt` so
non-English locales fell back to English. 11 of 16 locales had
already shipped real translations for them; only 4 cells needed
a value:

- de: Hot → Beliebt, Classic → Klassiker
- es: Hot → Populares
- it: Hot → Popolari
- nl: Hot → Populair

"Hot" reuses each locale's existing `exploreTabPopular`
translation, matching the pattern am/ar/id/ja/ko/tr already use
where Hot and Popular collapse to the same word.

Removes the 5 keys from `_knownUntranslatedDebt`; refs #3814.

fix(safety): default Divine-hosted-only filter to enabled (#4076)

only videos served from *.divine.video hosts we can moderate. Users
opt in to the wider Nostr media-host space by toggling
"Only show Divine-hosted videos" off in Settings → Content & Safety.
Users who already explicitly disabled the toggle keep their stored
preference.
